However, it reconstructs neither the modeled material nor the central mechanism. The generated hypothesis instead attributes behavior to deformation twinning in a polycrystalline specimen at experimentally accessible rates. It also misses the target predictions of temperature-induced yield softening, yield-strength insensitivity to strain rate, increasing dislocation density and flow stress with rate, and crystallographic anisotropy. Because the main mechanism is contradicted by the actual result and has no supporting evidence, the hypothesis is unsupported relative to the hidden target despite having a reasonably discriminating experiment.
